title: streaming-prefetch-rerank-budget-recycling-and-soft-deadlines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a streaming prefetch + budget-recycling strategy for the reranking endpoint to reduce tail latency while preserving overall token efficiency and quality. This ticket covers design, prototype, perf evaluation, and staged rollout.

Motivation: Current reranker suffers from high 95/99p latency when candidate documents have variable token lengths and when KV cache misses cause single-request stalls. Simple microbatching and fixed token caps reduce throughput or harm quality for longer candidates. We need a mechanism that: 1) starts useful work early for long-running candidates, 2) reallocates unused token budget from short candidates to ones that would otherwise timeout, and 3) gracefully degrades output when deadlines approach.

Key ideas:
- Streaming prefetch: immediately begin embedding/candidate KV prefetch for top-N candidates in a prioritized, nonblocking stream while the main request is being assembled. Prefetch operates at per-candidate granularity and updates a local KV cache shared across concurrent rerank requests.
- Token-granular micro-slices: for generation-based scorers, schedule candidates in small token slices (e.g., 8-16 tokens) so longer candidates make incremental progress and partial scores can be produced quickly.
- Budget recycling: allocate a per-request token budget (configurable). When a candidate finishes early (consumes fewer tokens), recycle the leftover token budget to active candidates that are closest to producing a final score.
- Soft deadlines and confidence early-exit: attach a heuristic confidence estimator to partial scores. If confidence crosses threshold before token budget exhausted, emit final score early. Conversely, if deadline approaches, produce best-effort score from partial state and mark as fallback.
- Backpressure-aware routing: expose a fast-path routing policy that will prefer cached-KV hosts for latency-sensitive reranks and fall back to throughput hosts for best-effort scoring.

Acceptance criteria:
- P95 latency reduction >= 15% on synthetic mixed-length workload compared to baseline microbatching.
- P99 latency reduction >= 10% while maintaining candidate ordering quality (NDCG@10 drop <= 0.5%).
- No customer-facing errors introduced during canary rollout.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: deep model changes to the scorer, global quota plumbing, and UI changes in Console (observability widgets will be added in follow-ups).
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after spike. Prototype prototype/stream-prefetch branch has basic prefetch + micro-slicing for the llama-reranker model. See design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/123456789/Streaming+Prefetch+Rerank

2026-03-02 - Liam Chen: Implemented local KV prefetch table and per-request token budget accounting. Running unit tests and local perf harness. Initial manual test: p95 improved ~18% on 256 candidate mix with median candidate length 120 tokens.

2026-03-03 - Anjali Rao (reviewer): Code review feedback: 1) add guardrails for budget underflow; 2) instrument per-candidate recycled tokens; 3) ensure prefetch doesn't starve normal request processing. Left comments in PR.

2026-03-04 - Liam Chen: Addressed review feedback. Added metrics: rerank.prefetch.kv_hit, rerank.budget.recycled_tokens, rerank.soft_exit.count. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421

2026-03-05 - Eng Ops (Kenji Morales): Ran throughput run on canary rack. Observations: P95 down 22%, P99 down 9%, cost delta +3%. Noted an increase in KV churn in one host — need eviction policy tweak before wide rollout.

2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Decision log: proceed with staged canary (10% of rerank traffic) with eviction policy change: prefer LRU by token-length and age. Follow-up ticket planned to add Console dashboard for recycled-token heatmaps.
